title: Adaptive first-session checklist carousel + contextual empty-state variants for Console
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Design a compact, skippable "first-session" checklist presented as a horizontally swipeable carousel and tie each checklist step to contextual empty states throughout the Redwood Console. Deliverables: annotated Figma frames for the carousel (desktop/tablet/mobile), 3 empty-state variants for key Console surfaces, a screenshot-ready set for release notes, and handoff tokens for engineering (spacing, motion timings, accessibility notes).

Scope and constraints: keep the component lightweight (no heavy network calls on first render), support keyboard navigation and screen readers, integrate with existing Console state (user_has_created_workspace, user_has_made_first_api_call, user_has_added_team_member). The carousel must support both a compact 'banner' placement at the top of primary dashboards and a modal-first-run for air-gapped/private installs where persistent banner is disabled.

Out of scope: deep walkthrough overlays (we'll link to existing overlays project for that) and multi-step guided prompts that require server-side progress tracking (engineers will add tracking in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Carousel variant implemented for desktop and mobile with keyboard and screen-reader support
At least three contextual empty-state variants produced and exported as 2x/3x PNGs for release assets
Design tokens and motion specs documented in Figma and included in handoff doc
Accessibility notes (aria roles, focus order) added and reviewed by accessibility engineer
Edge-case flows documented: user returns after partial completion, user in private deployment (no external links)
screenshots_needed: Banner carousel at top of Workloads dashboard (desktop, 1200px)
Mobile carousel in workspace overview (iPhone 13 frame)
Empty-state: workspace list (no projects) - light/dark variants
Empty-state: API credentials page (first key) - with callout
Empty-state for Dedicated customers (private deployment) without external docs links
empty_state_variants: Starter — primary CTA to create the first workspace, short benefit copy, small illustration
Guided — two CTAs: create workspace or follow quickstart template, step indicator
Hands-off — for enterprise/private installs: inline interstitial with local docs link and contact admin CTA
tour_steps: Step 1: Welcome card — brief value prop + dismissible checkbox 'don't show again'
Step 2: Create workspace CTA — quick action with inline small form (name only)
Step 3: Add API key shortcut — direct link to 'Create API Key' modal
Step 4: Try sample request — sample curl prefilled with user's region/model and copy button
Step 5: Next steps — links to Console tour and console docs; skip button and 'remind me later' option
decisions: Use a horizontal carousel (swipe + arrow) rather than a vertical list to conserve vertical real estate on dashboards
Default to non-modal banner on hosted Console; fall back to modal in private deployments where banner injection isn't permitted
Keep external doc links behind environment check; show self-hosted doc URLs when platform provides them
Animations: 240ms ease-out for slide transitions; reduced-motion respects OS setting
tradeoffs: Carousel vs. persistent checklist column: carousel is less discoverable over long term but minimizes layout churn and is easier to A/B test
Including inline forms reduces friction but adds validation complexity — decision to keep forms minimal (name/email only)
Embedding sample curl could expose region/model info; we'll sanitize dynamic tokens on initial render
